title: Log the Auto-Approval
scenario: It is 11:35 AM. The match decision routed INV-58831 to auto-approve. No human will look at it - and that is the point of a clean pipeline. But 'no human looked' is not the same as 'no record exists.' Learn what the auto-approve path must log so an automatic approval is still fully accountable.
input: Match decision: route auto-approve (within tolerance, quantities matched, not a duplicate). The auto-approve path releases INV-58831 toward the payment batch without human review, and writes an auto-approval log entry: invoice, why it qualified, the policy version applied, and the timestamp.
instructions: Read the auto-approve path as a straight-through handoff, not a rubber stamp.
Answer the four questions about accountability without a human.
Validate to mint the auto-approval log entry.

questions.prompt: What does the auto-approve path do with INV-58831?

options.text: Holds it for a manager to sign
Releases it toward the payment batch without human review
Sends it back to the vendor

questions.explain: A clean match earns straight-through processing: the invoice moves toward payment automatically. That speed is the payoff of getting the earlier checks right.

questions.prompt: If no human approves it, how is the approval still accountable?

options.text: It is not - automatic approvals cannot be audited
The path logs why it qualified and which policy version it applied
The vendor keeps the record instead

questions.explain: Accountability comes from the log, not a signature. Recording the qualifying reasons and the policy version means an auditor can reconstruct exactly why the system approved it.

questions.prompt: Why record the tolerance policy version in the log?

options.text: So a later auditor knows which rule was in force at the time
It has no purpose; the version never changes
To bill the vendor for the check

questions.explain: Policies change. Stamping v1.0.0 into the log freezes which rule approved this invoice, so a decision made today still makes sense after the policy is revised.

questions.prompt: Where does the invoice go next from here?
questions.explain: Auto-approved invoices flow to the Payment Batch, where the day's approved payments are gathered before the run. The exception queue joins there too, from the other path.

successMessage: Auto-approval logged. INV-58831 moves toward the batch - and the record explains exactly why, no signature needed.

sections.title: Straight-through is the reward
sections.body: A clean match earns automatic release - the invoice moves toward payment with no human in the loop. Speed on the clean cases is the whole reason to invest in the checks.

sections.title: Automatic is not unaccountable
sections.body: No human signed, but a record still must exist. The path logs the invoice, why it qualified, and which policy it applied - accountability lives in the log, not a signature.

sections.title: Freeze the rule that was applied
sections.body: Stamping the tolerance policy version (v1.0.0) into the log means a future auditor knows which rule was in force. When the policy changes, today's decision still makes sense.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: An auto-approval log entry: the invoice, the qualifying reasons, the policy version, and the timestamp - the evidence that a machine approval was justified.
